comment: Capability slice for the connectivity / time / audio / button build group. Every state is drawn from the mission's allowed terminal-state set. NOTHING here is VERIFIED_ON_S10PLUS: no item in this file is based on an observation made on the handset during this run. A passing offline test is OFFLINE_TESTED and stays OFFLINE_TESTED.

items.why_this_state: The default state is BLOCKED_FIRMWARE because nothing in this repository has observed a BCM4375-class radio binding, loading firmware or associating on the handset. The state is evidence-derived at runtime by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-wifi-diag.sh; BLOCKED_FIRMWARE is the *default* claim, not the *measured* one, and it is deliberately pessimistic: an unproven radio must never be advertised as working.
evidence_required_for_promotion: nuxelctl wifi status prints verdict=ASSOCIATED with a non-empty IPv4 address on the handset
a page loads in the Nuxel browser and the link survives 10 idle minutes
/var/log/nuxel/wifi-diag.log pre- and post-run blocks attached to the report
items.device_note: S10+ carries a Murata/Broadcom BCM4375-class part. docs/wifi-bcm4390-status.md describes the Pixel BCM4390 and was explicitly NOT applied to this device (no blob name, quirk or conclusion copied).

items.why_this_state: NetworkManager device/connection policy, the supplicant parameters, the credential-free connection template and the read-mostly diagnostic are all covered by tools/s10plus/a33/tests/test-wifi-diag.py and five faked-root fixtures. No credential is stored, no partition is written.

The RTC device naming on this PMIC is enumerated at runtime, never assumed, and the read/write path is exercised through the mark/compare pair. Until the owner records that pair on the handset, the RTC is unobserved.

Persistence is only proven by a before/after pair across one ordinary reboot with a changed boot id. The repository ships the procedure and the arithmetic; it cannot perform the reboot on the owner's behalf, and it must not repeat the reboot on failure (no blind repeat reboots).
evidence_required_for_promotion: nuxelctl time mark before the reboot and nuxelctl time compare after it, both quoted in the report
compare returns PASS with the RTC and wall-clock deltas stated
independent reference clock agrees within 60 s

items.why_this_state: The policy prefers systemd-timesyncd and documents chrony as the fallback, but the tool probes for the real unit on the real image and reports NO_TIMESYNC_BACKEND rather than pretending a sync is running. Only the socket/unit probe and the fixture verdict logic are tested offline; the running backend on the handset is NEEDS_OWNER_TEST.
evidence: python3 tools/s10plus/a33/tests/test-time-rtc.py -> all checks PASS (incl. NO_TIMESYNC_BACKEND fixture)

items.why_this_state: The UCM2 master profile is anchored on the real ALSA card name beyond-madera, the PipeWire/WirePlumber drops and the ALSA softvol ceiling are installed configuration, and the pipeline walker plus its fixtures are tested offline. The sequences are deliberately empty and are generated from a *captured* control list, because inventing MADEERA/CS47L93 control names would be a fabrication.

A writable mixer control is explicitly NOT an acceptance criterion for this mission. Whether the CS35L40 amplifiers and the CS47L93 DAC actually produce sound is an observation only a human ear can make, and it is deferred by design.
evidence_required_for_promotion: owner confirms the low-volume test tone is heard from the speaker
the pipeline walker reports the DAC/DAPM stages running (not silent) while the tone plays

items.why_this_state: Jack-insert and USB-C accessory detection are implemented as evidence-derived state (ALSA jack kcontrols, /proc/asound/*/codec#* pin state, ALSA card enumeration for a UAC device, /sys/class/typec) and are exercised offline against fixtures. Audibility through a real adapter remains NEEDS_OWNER_TEST.
Requires a human to plug in headphones or a USB-C adapter and listen. Deferred by design; this item must never gate another briQ.

The A32 release record documents the button manager as the single owner of gpio_keys and the display toggle / ALSA volume / assistant-key behaviour as observed on the handset (docs/s10plus-autonomous-boot-repair/BETA-HARDWARE-FINALIZER/13-RELEASE-NOTES-A32.md). That observation is the A32 floor and is preserved byte-identically by this group (a32 sources are untouched, and tools/beta/regression-guard.sh INV-4 keeps them pinned).

The A33 state machine (single/double/long press classes, very-long-press reboot gate, power menu with Recovery / Download-Mode entries, screen-gesture recognizer) is implemented and offline-tested but has not been installed on the handset or observed there. It is NOT a claim that the new behaviour works on the phone.
evidence: cc -std=c11 -fsyntax-only tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-button-fsm.h harness (offline FSM compile + replay)
A32 behavioural parity assertions (press windows and repeat cadence extracted from the protected A32 source) PASS

items.why_this_state: The power menu exists as a state machine with Recovery and Download-Mode entries that can be selected and offline-tested but are hard-refused at execution time (they require an owner-typed confirmation and are never triggered by this mission). The refusal, not the entry, is what is tested.
evidence: python3 tools/s10plus/a33/tests/test-button-fsm.py (recovery/download refused; no flashing surface in the manager)
tool contains no heimdall / odin / fastboot / /dev/block / dd path

items.why_this_state: The gesture state machine (swipe-up home, swipe-up-hold recents, edge back) is implemented in the dependency-free FSM core and replayed offline against recorded event traces. Dispatch is to the launcher's own control FIFO and is idempotent, so it cannot double-fire against the launcher's own touch handling.
